replacement_value.claim: (Mackey filtration.) Fix a second flag with idempotent $e'=e(\beta',\gamma')$ and choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row block permutation group and the column block permutation group acting on the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ positions. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner $eAe'$ by the four intersection blocks $(a,b;c,d)$ with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, and filter by the crossing length of the double-coset representatives. The span of the double cosets of strictly smaller length is a $(B,B')$-sub-bimodule: sliding a block generator across a representative either stays in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or produces a quadratic/braid correction of strictly smaller length, which lies in the smaller span. In the associated quotient only the monomials whose permutation is the minimal double-coset representative survive; they are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases of the four blocks composed with the row and column induced bimodules and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks, which carries the shift $-(b\mid c)$ because the crossed colours are precisely $b$ and $c$. The basis bijection defines inverse maps between the associated quotient and the composite four-block restriction/induction bimodule, so the filtration is proved and not merely a character identity; iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block statement.

(Triangularity and the functor formula.) Pair the right $B$-module shuffle basis of $Ae'$ (through the block flip) with the left $B$-module shuffle basis of $eA$ by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, the coefficient matrix of the pairing $u\mapsto t(uz)$ is triangular: a complementary pair is exactly the reduced longest shuffle with coefficient $1$ up to the absorbed equal-colour signs, and a noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic or braid correction to strictly smaller length, hence vanishes in the associated graded. Finite triangular elimination over $B$ (division by the diagonal units $1$) inverts the matrix, so $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of graded $(A,B)$-bimodules; consequently $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\cong Ae'\{c\}$ with the $B$-action transported by the block flip. Since $eA$ is finite projective over $B$ by step 1.1, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\otimes_BX\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,X)$ for every graded $B$-module $X$ (checked on finite free modules and finite summands), and tracking the outer right $B$-action through the flip gives the functorial isomorphism $\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}$.

All clauses of the statement are now proved: step 1.1 gives the freeness and the labelled shuffle shifts, step 2.1 the exactness, shift compatibility and projective preservation, step 1.2 the left adjunction, steps 2.2 and 3.1 the right adjoint and its exact reversed-block formula, and step 2.3 the finite Mackey filtration and its multi-block version.
